kickable: Capable or deserving of being kicked. "A kickable boy." G. Eliot.
kitty: 1. A kitten; also, a pet name or calling name for the cat. 2. [Etym. uncertain.] (Gaming) The percentage taken out of a pool to pay for refreshments, or for the expenses of the table. R. F. Foster.
kistvaen: A Celtic monument, commonly known as a dolmen.
killdeer: A small American plover (Ægialitis vocifera). Note: It is dark grayish brown above; the rump and upper tail coverts are yellowish rufous; the belly, throat, and a line over the eyes, white; a ring round the neck and band across the breast, black.
kiva: A large chamber built under, or in, the houses of a Pueblo village, used as an assembly room in religious rites or as a men's dormitory. It is commonly lighted and entered from an opening in the roof.
kimnel: A tub. See Kemelin. (old) She knew not what a kimnel was Beau. & Fl.
kist: A chest; hence, a coffin. [Scot. & Prov. End.] Jamieson. Halliwell. | A stated payment, especially a payment of rent for land; hence, the time for such payment. [India]
kindless: Destitute of kindness; unnatural.(old) "Kindless villain." Shak.
kingpost: A member of a common form of truss, as a roof truss. It is strictly a tie, intended to prevent the sagging of the tiebeam in the middle. (Law) Formerly, the highest court of common law in England;
kingbird: 1. A small American bird (Tyrannus, or T. Carolinensis), noted for its courage in attacking larger birds, even hawks and eagles, especially when they approach its nest in the breeding season. kibed: Chapped; cracked with cold; affected with chilblains; as kibed heels. Beau. & Fl.
kindle: To bring forth young. (old) Shak. The poor beast had but lately kindled. Holland. | 1. To set on fire; to cause to burn with flame; to ignite; to cause to begin burning; to start; to light; as, to kindle a match, or shavings. His breath kindleth coals. Job xii. 21. 2.
kinglet: 1. A little king; a weak or insignificant king. Carlyle. 2. (Zoöl.) Any one of several species of small singing birds of the genus Regulus and family Sylviidæ. Note: The golden-crowned kinglet (Regulus satrapa), and the rubycrowned kinglet (R. calendula), are the most common American species. The common English kinglet (R.
kingfisher: Any one of numerous species of birds constituting the family Alcedinidæ. Most of them feed upon fishes which they capture by diving and seizing then with the beak; others feed only upon reptiles, insects, etc. About one hundred and fifty species are known. They are found in nearly all parts of the world, but are particularly abundant in the East Indies.
kiss: 1. To salute with the lips, as a mark of affection, reverence, submission, forgiveness, etc. He . . . kissed her lips with such a clamorous smack, That at the parting all the church echoed. Shak. 2. | 1. To make or give salutation with the lips in token of love, respect, etc.; as, kiss and make friends. 2. To meet; to come in contact; to touch fondly. Like fire and powder, Which as they kiss…
kicksywicksy: That which is restless and uneasy. Note: Kicky-wicky, or, in some editions, Kicksy-wicksy, is applied contemptuously to a wife by Shakespeare, in "All's Well that Ends Well," ii. 3, 297. | Fantastic; restless; as, kicksy-wicksy flames. Nares.
kier: A large tub or vat in which goods are subjected to the action of hot lye or bleaching liquor; -- also called keeve.
kissingstrings: Cap or bonnet strings made long to tie under the chin. One of her ladyship's kissing strings, once pink and fluttering and now faded and soiled. Pall Mall Mag.
kirmess: In Europe, particularly in Belgium and Holland, and outdoor festival and fair; in the United States, generally an indoor entertainment and fair combined.
kinepox: See Cowpox. Kin"e*scope (, n. See Kinetoscope.
kiver: To cover. -- n. A cover. [Disused except in illiterate speech.]
king: A Chinese musical instrument, consisting of resonant stones or metal plates, arranged according to their tones in a frame of wood, and struck with a hammer. | 1. A chief ruler; a sovereign; one invested with supreme authority over a nation, country, or tribe, usually by hereditary succession; a monarch; a prince. "Ay, every inch a king." Shak.
kingston: The black angel fish. See Angel fish, under Angel.
kitchenmiddens: Relics of neolithic man found on the coast of Denmark, consisting of shell mounds, some of which are ten feet high, one thousand feet long, and two hundred feet wide. The name is applied also to similar mounds found on the American coast from Canada to Florida, made by the North American Indians.
kidney: 1. (Anat.) A glandular organ which excretes urea and other waste products from the animal body; a urinary gland. kilogram: A measure of weight, being a thousand grams, equal to 2.2046 pounds avoirdupois (15,432.34 grains). It is equal to the weight of a cubic decimeter of distilled water at the temperature of maximum density, or 39º Fahrenheit.
kirkman: 1. A clergyman or officer in a kirk. [Scot.] 2. A member of the Church of Scotland, as distinguished from a member of another communion. [Scot.]
kingtruss: A truss, framed with a king-post; -- used in roofs, bridges, etc.
kith: Acquaintance; kindred. And my near kith for sore me shend. W. Browne. The sage of his kith and the hamlet. Longfellow. Kith and kin, kindred more or less remote.
kirk: A church or the church, in the various senses of the word; esp., the Church of Scotland as distinguished from other reformed churches, or from the Roman Catholic Church. [Scot.] Jamieson.
kiefekil: A species of clay; meerschaum. [Also written keffekil.]
kippernut: A name given to earthnuts of several kinds.
kinesthetic: Of, pertaining to, or involving, kinæsthesis.
kingstonmetal: . An alloy of tin, copper, and mercury, sometimes used for the bearings and packings of machinery. McElrath.
kibe: A chap or crack in the flesh occasioned by cold; an ulcerated chilblain. "He galls his kibe." Shak.
kinetophone: A machine combining a kinetoscope and a phonograph synchronized so as to reproduce a scene and its accompanying sounds.
kinkajou: A nocturnal carnivorous mammal (Cercoleptes caudivolvulus) of South America, about as large as a full-grown cat. It has a prehensile tail and lives in trees. It is the only representative of a distinct family (Cercoleptidæ) allied to the raccoons. Called also potto, and honey bear.
killjoy: One who causes gloom or grief; a dispiriting person. W. Black.
kindness: 1. The state or quality of being kind, in any of its various senses; manifestation of kind feeling or disposition beneficence. I do fear thy nature; It is too full o' the milk of human kindness To catch the nearest way. Shak. Unremembered acts Of kindness and of love. Wordsworth. 2. A kind act; an act of good will; as, to do a great kindness. Syn. -- Good will; benignity;
kinematic: Of or pertaining to kinematics. Kinematic curves, curves produced by machinery, or a combination of motions, as distinguished from mathematical curves.
kingcharlesspaniel: A variety of small pet dogs, having, drooping ears, a high, dome-shaped forehead, pug nose, large, prominent eyes, and long, wavy hair. The color is usually black and tan.
kindergartner: One who teaches in a kindergarten.
kitchenmaid: A woman employed in the kitchen. Shak.
kindhearted: Having kindness of nature; sympathetic; characterized by a humane disposition; as, a kind-hearted landlord. To thy self at least kind-hearted prove. Shak.
kilnhole: The mouth or opening of an oven or kiln. Shak.
kinetoscope: A machine, for the production of animated pictures, in which a film carrying successive instantaneous views of a moving scene travels uniformly through the field of a magnifying glass. kilogrammetre: A measure of energy or work done, being the amount expended in raising one kilogram through the height of one meter, in the latitude of Paris.
kingstone: The black angel fish. See Angel fish, under Angel.
kingstonvalve: A conical valve, opening outward, to close the mouth of a pipe which passes through the side of a vessel below the water line.
kilolitre: A measure of capacity equal to a cubic meter, or a thousand liters. It is equivalent to 35.315 cubic feet, and to 220.04 imperial gallons, or 264.18 American gallons of 321 cubic inches.
kilogramme: A measure of weight, being a thousand grams, equal to 2.2046 pounds avoirdupois (15,432.34 grains). It is equal to the weight of a cubic decimeter of distilled water at the temperature of maximum density, or 39º Fahrenheit.
kiosk: A Turkish open summer house or pavilion, supported by pillars.
kilo: A combining form used to signify thousand in forming the names of units of measurement; as, kilogram, kilometer, kilowatt, etc.
kincob: India silk brocaded with flowers in silver or gold. -- a. Of the nature of kincob; brocaded. Thackeray.
kinit: A unit of force equal to the force which, acting for one second, will give a pound a velocity of one foot per second; -- proposed by J.D.Everett, an English physicist.

kindler: One who, or that which, kindles, stirs up, or sets on fire."Kindlers of riot." Gay.
kieserite: Hydrous sulphate of magnesia found at the salt mines of Stassfurt, Prussian Saxony.
kilogrammeter: A measure of energy or work done, being the amount expended in raising one kilogram through the height of one meter, in the latitude of Paris.
kidderminster: A kind of ingrain carpeting, named from the English town where formerly most of it was manufactured.
kinetograph: (a) A camera for making chronophotographs. (b) A machine for the projection of chronophotographs upon a screen for the purpose of producing the effect of an animated picture. kitchenette: A room combining a very small kitchen and a pantry, with the kitchen conveniences compactly arranged, sometimes so that they fold up out of sight and allow the kitchen to be made a part of the adjoining room by opening folding doors.
kine: Cows. "A herd of fifty or sixty kine." Milton.
kickywisky: That which is restless and uneasy. Note: Kicky-wicky, or, in some editions, Kicksy-wicksy, is applied contemptuously to a wife by Shakespeare, in "All's Well that Ends Well," ii. 3, 297.
kirtle: A garment varying in form and use at different times, and worn doth by men and women. Wearing her Norman car, and her kirtle of blue. Longfellow. Note: The term is still retained in the provinces, in the sense of " an outer petticoat." Halliwell.
kithe: To make known; to manifest; to show; to declare. [Obs: or Scot.] For gentle hearte kytheth gentilesse. Chaucer.
kilometer: A measure of length, being a thousand meters. It is equal to 3,280.8 feet, or 62137 of a mile.
kilostere: A cubic measure containing 1000 cubic meters, and equivalent to 35,315 cubic feet.

kinaesthesis: The perception attendant upon the movements of the muscles. Bastian.
kiddy: To deceive; to outwit; to hoax. [Slang] Dickens. | A young fellow; formerly, a low thief. [Slang, Eng.]
kitchenry: The body of servants employed in the kitchen. (old) Holland.

kicker: One who, or that which, kicks.
killow: An earth of a blackish or deep blue color. Woodward.

kinematical: Of or pertaining to kinematics. Kinematic curves, curves produced by machinery, or a combination of motions, as distinguished from mathematical curves.
killigrew: The Cornish chough. See under Chough. [Prov. Eng. & Scot.]
kinetogenesis: An instrument for producing curves by the combination of circular movements; -- called also kinescope.
kilometre: A measure of length, being a thousand meters. It is equal to 3,280.8 feet, or 62137 of a mile.
kickup: The water thrush or accentor. [Local, West Indies]
kid: 1. (Zoöl.) A young goat. The . . . leopard shall lie down with the kid. Is. xi. 6 . 2. A young child or infant; hence, a simple person, easily imposed on. [Slang] Charles Reade. 3. | A fagot; a bundle of heath and furze. [Prov. Eng.] Wright.

kilerg: A unit of work equal to one thousand ergs.
kidneyshaped: Having the form or shape of a kidney; reniform; as, a kidney- shaped leaf. Gray.
kinaesthetic: Of, pertaining to, or involving, kinæsthesis.

kimbo: Crooked; arched; bent. [Written also kimbow.] Dryden.
kipe: An osier basket used for catching fish. [Prov. Eng.]
kickshaws: 1. Something fantastical; any trifling, trumpery thing; a toy. Art thou good at these kickshawses! Shak. 2. A fancy dish; a titbit; a delicacy. Some pigeons, . . . a joint of mutton, and any pretty little tiny kickshaws. Shak. Cressy was lost by kickshaws and soup-maigre. Fenton.
kipskin: Leather prepared from the skin of young or small cattle, intermediate in grade between calfskin and cowhide.
kissingcrust: The portion of the upper crust of a loaf which has touched another loaf in baking. Lamb. A massy fragment from the rich kissingcrust that hangs like a fretted cornice from the upper half of the loaf. W. Howitt.
kilowatthour: A unit of work or energy equal to that done by one kilowatt acting for one hour; --approx. = 1.34 horse-power hour.
kinesodic: Conveying motion; as; kinesodic substance; -- applied esp. to the spinal cord, because it is capable of conveying doth voluntary and reflex motor impulses, without itself being affected by motor impulses applied to it directly.
kidneywort: (a) A kind of saxifrage (Saxifrage stellaris). (b) The navelwort.
kinesiatrics: A mode of treating disease by appropriate muscular movements; - - also termed kinesitherapy, kinesipathy, lingism, and the movement cure.
kink: 1. A twist or loop in a rope or thread, caused by a spontaneous doubling or winding upon itself; a close loop or curl; a doubling in a cord. 2. An unreasonable notion; a crotchet; a whim; a caprice. | To wind into a kink; to knot or twist spontaneously upon itself, as a rope or thread.
kilting: A perpendicular arrangement of flat, single plaits, each plait being folded so as to cover half the breadth of the preceding one.
kiwikiwi: Any species of Apteryx, esp. A. australis; -- so called in imitation of its notes. Called also kiwi. See Apteryx.
kirked: Turned upward; bent. (old) Rom. of R.
killdee: A small American plover (Ægialitis vocifera). Note: It is dark grayish brown above; the rump and upper tail coverts are yellowish rufous; the belly, throat, and a line over the eyes, white; a ring round the neck and band across the breast, black.
kissingbug: Any one of several species of blood-sucking, venomous Hemiptera that sometimes bite the lip or other parts of the human body, causing painful sores, as the cone-nose (Conorhinus sanguisuga). [U. S.]

kirsome: Christian; christened. (old) I am a true kirsome woman. Beau. & Fl.

kinky: 1. Full of kinks; liable to kink or curl; as, kinky hair. 2. Queer; eccentric; crotchety. [Colloq. U.S.]

kioways: A tribe of Indians distantly related to the Shoshones. They formerly inhabited the region about the head waters of the North Platte.
kilovolt: A unit of electromotive force equal to one thousand volts.
kilted: 1. Having on a kilt. 2. Plaited after the manner of kilting. 3. Tucked or fastened up; -- said of petticoats, etc.
kimono: 1. A kind of loose robe or gown tied with a sash, worn as an outer garment by Japanese men and women. 2. A similar gown worn as a dressing gown by women of Western nations.
kibblings: Portions of small fish used for bait on the banks of Newfoundland.
kidnapper: One who steals or forcibly carries away a human being; a manstealer.

kidneyform: Having the form or shape of a kidney; reniform; as, a kidney- shaped leaf. Gray.

kilt: p. p. from Kill. (old) Spenser. | A kind of short petticoat, reaching from the waist to the knees, worn in the Highlands of Scotland by men, and in the Lowlands by young boys; a filibeg. [Written also kelt.]
kinghood: The state of being a king; the attributes of a king; kingship. Gower.

kieselguhr: Siliceous earth; specifically, porous infusorial earth, used as an absorbent of nitroglycerin in the manufacture of dynamite.
kinology: That branch of physics which treats of the laws of motion, or of moving bodies.
kiloliter: A measure of capacity equal to a cubic meter, or a thousand liters. It is equivalent to 35.315 cubic feet, and to 220.04 imperial gallons, or 264.18 American gallons of 321 cubic inches.
kivikivi: Any species of Apteryx, esp. A. australis; -- so called in imitation of its notes. Called also kiwi. See Apteryx.

kitten: To bring forth young, as a cat; to bring forth, as kittens. Shak. H. Spencer.
